# Automata Simulator — Full LLM Reference

> A web-based visual editor and simulator for finite automata (DFA and NFA).
> URL: https://automata.yuweiss.dev
> Source: https://github.com/YuvalWS/automata-simulator
> Summary: https://automata.yuweiss.dev/llms.txt

## JSON Schema (Zod Definitions)

The app validates loaded files using these Zod schemas:

```typescript
const PointSchema = z.object({
  x: z.number(),
  y: z.number(),
});

const ViewportSchema = z.object({
  panX: z.number(),
  panY: z.number(),
  zoom: z.number().positive(),  // must be > 0
});

const AutomatonStateSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  position: PointSchema,
  isInitial: z.boolean(),
  isAccepting: z.boolean(),
});

const TransitionSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
  sourceId: z.string().min(1),
  targetId: z.string().min(1),
  symbols: z.array(z.string()),
  controlPointOffset: PointSchema.optional(),
});

const AutomatonSchema = z.object({
  id: z.string().min(1),
  name: z.string().min(1),
  type: z.enum(['DFA', 'NFA']),
  alphabet: z.array(z.string()),
  states: z.array(AutomatonStateSchema),
  transitions: z.array(TransitionSchema),
  viewport: ViewportSchema,
});

const SaveFileSchema = z.object({
  version: z.string(),
  automaton: AutomatonSchema,
});
```

## Field Reference

### SaveFile
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| version | string | File format version, currently `"1.0.0"` |
| automaton | Automaton | The automaton data |

### Automaton
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| id | string (min 1) | Unique identifier for the automaton |
| name | string (min 1) | Display name shown in the UI |
| type | `"DFA"` or `"NFA"` | Automaton type |
| alphabet | string[] | List of input symbols (excluding ε) |
| states | State[] | Array of states |
| transitions | Transition[] | Array of transitions |
| viewport | Viewport | Camera position and zoom level |

### State
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| id | string (min 1) | Unique identifier |
| name | string (min 1) | Display label (e.g., "q0", "q1") |
| position | {x, y} | Canvas coordinates for visual layout |
| isInitial | boolean | Whether this is the start state (exactly one should be true) |
| isAccepting | boolean | Whether this is an accepting/final state |

### Transition
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| id | string (min 1) | Unique identifier |
| sourceId | string (min 1) | ID of the source state |
| targetId | string (min 1) | ID of the target state (same as sourceId for self-loops) |
| symbols | string[] | Symbols that trigger this transition |
| controlPointOffset | {x, y}? | Optional offset for curved rendering |

### Viewport
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| panX | number | Horizontal pan offset |
| panY | number | Vertical pan offset |
| zoom | number (> 0) | Zoom level (1.0 = 100%) |

## Validation Rules

### DFA-specific rules
- Each state must have at most one transition per input symbol (no nondeterminism)
- Epsilon transitions (`"ε"`, U+03B5) are not allowed
- Ideally, every state has a transition for every symbol in the alphabet (the app warns about missing transitions)

### NFA-specific rules
- Multiple transitions from the same state on the same symbol are allowed
- Epsilon transitions are allowed — use the symbol `"ε"` (U+03B5)
- During simulation, epsilon-closure is computed automatically

### General rules
- Exactly one state must have `isInitial: true`
- All `sourceId` and `targetId` must reference valid state IDs
- The `alphabet` array should list all symbols used in transitions (ε is excluded from the alphabet)
- IDs must be non-empty strings (UUIDs are commonly used but any non-empty string works)

## Layout Tips

When generating automata for visual display:
- Space states ~200px apart horizontally for readability
- A typical Y coordinate is 200-300 for a single row
- For multi-row layouts, use ~200px vertical spacing
- The viewport `{ panX: 0, panY: 0, zoom: 1 }` is a good default
- State names conventionally use "q0", "q1", "q2", etc.

## Example 1: DFA that accepts strings ending with "ab"

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "dfa-ends-ab",
    "name": "Ends with ab",
    "type": "DFA",
    "alphabet": ["a", "b"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "q0", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "q1", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s2", "name": "q2", "position": { "x": 500, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": true }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["b"] },
      { "id": "t2", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t3", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s2", "symbols": ["b"] },
      { "id": "t4", "sourceId": "s2", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t5", "sourceId": "s2", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["b"] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 }
  }
}
```

## Example 2: NFA with epsilon transitions (accepts "a*b*")

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "nfa-a-star-b-star",
    "name": "a*b* (NFA with ε)",
    "type": "NFA",
    "alphabet": ["a", "b"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "q0", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true, "isAccepting": false },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "q1", "position": { "x": 300, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": true }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["ε"] },
      { "id": "t2", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["b"] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 }
  }
}
```

## Example 3: DFA with self-loop (accepts even number of a's)

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "automaton": {
    "id": "dfa-even-a",
    "name": "Even number of a's",
    "type": "DFA",
    "alphabet": ["a", "b"],
    "states": [
      { "id": "s0", "name": "even", "position": { "x": 100, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": true, "isAccepting": true },
      { "id": "s1", "name": "odd", "position": { "x": 350, "y": 200 }, "isInitial": false, "isAccepting": false }
    ],
    "transitions": [
      { "id": "t0", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t1", "sourceId": "s0", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["b"] },
      { "id": "t2", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s0", "symbols": ["a"] },
      { "id": "t3", "sourceId": "s1", "targetId": "s1", "symbols": ["b"] }
    ],
    "viewport": { "panX": 0, "panY": 0, "zoom": 1 }
  }
}
```

## How to Use Generated JSON

1. Save the JSON to a `.json` file
2. Open https://automata.yuweiss.dev
3. Click "Load" (or press Ctrl+O) and select the file
4. The automaton will render with all states, transitions, and layout preserved

## Describing Automata in Natural Language

When asked to explain an automaton JSON file:
1. Identify the type (DFA/NFA) and the alphabet
2. Identify the initial state and accepting state(s)
3. Describe the transition function (which symbols move between which states)
4. Describe the language the automaton accepts in set-builder notation or plain English
5. Note any self-loops and their purpose
